No tests are visible in the packet.
The schema version is a fixed text value that must be kept in step with changes by hand.

terms.meaning: a Python data shape that checks the types of its fields when a record is created
a version label that tells consumers which layout of results they are reading
how serious a warning is: information, warning or error
a fixed list of named choices, such as the supported file formats

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Module purpose and schema version
sections.what: Introduces the shared data shapes that the ingestion layer returns, and sets the schema version to 1.0.
sections.why: Likely reason: one agreed format lets every reader return results the same way, and the version lets consumers detect layout changes.

sections.name: SourceFormat
sections.title: Supported schedule file types
sections.what: Lists the five formats the app accepts: XER, P6 XML, XLSX, CSV and TSV.
sections.why: Gives other code one fixed list to check against.
sections.watch_out: Adding a format here does not add a reader; the dispatch file must also change.

sections.name: WarningSeverity
sections.title: Warning severity levels
sections.what: Defines three levels for warnings: info, warning and error.
sections.why: Lets the app show how serious each message is.

sections.name: IngestionWarning
sections.title: Single warning record
sections.what: Describes one warning with a code, a message, a severity, and optional table, row and extra detail fields. Any unexpected field is refused.
sections.why: Gives every warning the same shape so the app can list and filter them.
sections.watch_out: Because extra fields are refused, a new field must be added in every place a warning is built.

sections.name: WarningCollector
sections.title: Warning collector with limits
sections.what: Keeps the first examples of each warning type up to set limits, and counts the rest. When finished, it adds one summary line per warning type that was cut short.
sections.why: Likely reason: a file with huge numbers of bad rows must not fill memory or flood the report, while the true count is still kept.
sections.watch_out: The summary lines are added at the end and are not counted against the example limits.

sections.name: ProjectReference
sections.title: Project summary record
sections.what: Describes one project found in a file: its ID, name, date span, data date, and counts of activities that are dated, baseline, forecast or actual.
sections.why: Lets the app show a project list and its counts without re-reading the database.

sections.name: IngestionReport
sections.title: Full ingestion result record
sections.what: Describes everything an ingestion returns: source details, fingerprint, the staging database path, counts, projects, warnings, and flags for cancellation or needed column mapping. It also offers a helper that turns the stored path text into a path object, and a progress callback type is defined at the end.
sections.why: It is the single hand-off object between the parsers and the rest of the app.
sections.watch_out: The database path is stored as text, so the file must still exist when the report is used.

summary: Defines the shared data shapes that every schedule reader returns: warnings, project summaries and the full ingestion report.
purpose: Gives the parsers and the rest of the app one agreed format for results, so they can pass information without guessing its structure.
why: Strict shapes that refuse unexpected fields catch mistakes early. The warning collector keeps memory bounded when a file has very many problems.
how: The file defines the supported formats and severity levels, then a warning record, a collector that keeps a limited number of examples per warning type and counts the rest, a project summary record, and a final report record that combines everything an ingestion returns.
inputs: Values created by the readers in the ingest package, such as warnings, project details and counts.
outputs: Validated records of the types defined here, plus a combined list of warnings with summary lines for any that were cut short.
risks: Adding a field to a record requires updating every place that builds it, since extra fields are refused. Changing the schema version number without need can confuse consumers.
debug: If a report fails to build, check that every field a record needs is supplied and that no extra field was added. If warnings look incomplete, check the example limits in the collector.
